quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungary, September 6th marks the traditional end of harvest season, when families would celebrate with special pastries called 'rétes' (strudel) filled with apples, cherries, or poppyseeds. These delicate, paper-thin pastries were often shared with neighbors as a symbol of gratitude for the abundance of the earth.

short_read.title: The Secret Social Lives of Harbor Seals
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals in the Strait of Juan de Fuca have complex friendships that last for years, returning to the same haul-out spots to meet their companions. Scientists have discovered these playful marine mammals actually recognize each other's voices underwater.

medium_read.title: The Ancient Art of Saving Seeds
medium_read.teaser: For thousands of years, gardeners have saved seeds from their best plants to grow again next season, preserving flavors and varieties that might otherwise be lost. This heartwarming guide shows how easy it is to become part of this living tradition.

long_read.title: The Enchanted Rainforests of the Olympic Peninsula
long_read.teaser: The moss-draped temperate rainforests near Port Angeles are among the most magical places on Earth, where ancient trees create cathedral-like spaces and rainfall nurtures an ecosystem found almost nowhere else. This beautiful exploration reveals why these forests feel like stepping into another world.

port_angeles.title: Butterfly Season at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: Early September brings a final flutter of beautiful butterflies to Hurricane Ridge's wildflower meadows. Look for the vibrant orange-and-black Mylitta Crescents and delicate Pale Swallowtails dancing among the late-blooming asters and lupines before autumn settles in.

puzzle_1.question: The Olympic National Park, just south of Port Angeles, protects nearly ___ miles of wild Pacific coastline.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Perfect! That's right — 73 miles of beautiful, rugged coastline!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The park protects 73 miles of wild Pacific coast.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 73 miles — a stunning stretch of wilderness coastline protected forever!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: This pristine coastline includes sandy beaches, dramatic sea stacks, tide pools teeming with life, and some of the last truly wild shoreline in the continental United States.
puzzle_1.learn_more_label: Explore the Coast — National Park Service

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Gyönyörű! That's right — 'pillangó' is the Hungarian word for butterfly!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'pillangó' — such a beautiful word for such a delicate creature! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The word 'pillangó' comes from an old Hungarian root meaning 'to flutter' or 'to fly lightly,' perfectly capturing the graceful movement of these lovely insects.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree can live for over 1,000 years in the Pacific Northwest rainforests?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Western Red Cedar can indeed live for over 1,000 years — some ancient cedars in the Olympic Peninsula are over 1,500 years old!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is Western Red Cedar — these magnificent trees can live for over 1,000 years, with some ancient giants in the Olympic forests reaching 1,500 years old!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest call Western Red Cedar the 'Tree of Life' because it provided materials for canoes, longhouses, clothing, medicine, and countless other necessities for thousands of years.
